LMNA-581 · Lumina Care
TCM Daily Readmission Reports
Revision 2 · 15 September 2026

The readmission report behind a ten-minute code

What changed since the 9 September walkthrough, captured from the live sandbox after the rebuild. The public file link is gone. The email now opens a Lumina page that emails a six-digit code to the address on file, and every step on every link is logged with the time, the IP address and the browser.

BUILT & LIVE-TESTED IN SANDBOX · NOT YET IN PRODUCTION

A forwarded link, a copied URL or a screenshot no longer opens a report. Only the mailbox the report was sent to can get the code, and the code dies in ten minutes.

  • Chris's concern is closed: the link on its own is worthless, and every link is 256 bits of randomness, so guessing one is not possible.
  • Chayim's ask is built as asked: a one-time code that expires after ten minutes, requested when the report is opened rather than sent with it.
  • New since last time: an access log per link with IP address and browser, a hard view cap, automatic lockout after five wrong codes, and Lumina branding on every screen.
BackgroundThe 9 September build used a public expiring link. Chris asked for more than possession of the URL; Chayim asked for a ten-minute code.
StatusDeployed to the lumDev sandbox on 15 September. 142 of 142 automated tests pass. Every screen below is a real capture from a clean browser with no Salesforce login.
AskFour one-time steps in production, listed at the end, and a decision on the retention grace period. Nothing here has touched production.

Why a code at view time, not in the email

The report goes out on a schedule at 8am and nobody is waiting for it. Most people open it hours later, so a ten-minute code sent inside the report email would be dead before it was read. The page asks for the code at the moment of viewing instead, and sends it to the same address the report was issued to. That is also what makes a forwarded email useless: the code goes to the original mailbox, not to whoever is holding the link.

The happy path

Six steps, all captured on 15 September from the sandbox, in a browser with no Salesforce session, against a test facility with invented patients.

01

The job builds one report and one link per recipient

Unchanged in shape from last time: the nightly batch groups yesterday's readmissions by facility, renders that facility's report to PDF once, and issues a separate link per recipient. What changed is what a link is. It is no longer a public file URL. It is a row we own, holding only a scrambled copy of the secret in the URL, and it can be opened only through the Lumina page.

SettingValue in the tested run
Link lifetime24 hours, configurable. Same as before.
Code lifetime10 minutes from the moment it is sent.
View window after a correct code10 minutes. Reloading inside it shows the report again; after it, a new code is needed.
View cap10 opens per link. Now a hard cap, refused at the moment the eleventh code is entered, rather than a nightly check.
Wrong codes5 in total, then the link locks itself for good.
Code requestsAt most one a minute, and 5 per link, then the link locks.
Download allowedYes, logged separately from a view.
Public file linkRemoved. There is no URL that opens the PDF without a code.
02

Each recipient gets an email with no patient data and no secret in it

The message carries a count, a button, and one new line telling the recipient a code will be emailed when they open the link. Nothing in it opens the report on its own.

03

The link opens a Lumina page that shows nothing yet

No login, no account. The page names the facility and the report date, shows a masked version of the address on file so the reader knows where to look, and offers one button.

04

One click, and a six-digit code lands in that mailbox

The page emails a code to the address the link was issued to and switches to the code box. Asking again inside a minute is refused, so a stuck button cannot flood an inbox.

05

The right code opens the report; the wrong one costs a strike

A correct code counts one open, unlocks the report for ten minutes and shows the PDF on the page with a download button. A wrong code says how many attempts are left. The fifth wrong code locks the link permanently.

06

Everything that happened is on the record, with IP and browser

This is the new audit trail. Each link keeps counts as before, and now also an access log: one row per event with the time, the caller's IP address and browser, and a short note such as which attempt or which open it was.

What the audit answers now

The 9 September walkthrough had two honest gaps in this table. Both are closed.

Question9 SeptemberNowHow

A named human, not a mailboxPartlyYes, to the mailbox and the device A forwarded link no longer opens anything. Whoever opened it had the mailbox and the code in the same ten minutes
IP address of the viewerNoYes Every event on the link carries the caller's IP address and browser, on our own object, no add-on licence

The other paths

Every one of these was exercised live on 15 September, not only in automated tests.

07

Five wrong codes, or too many code requests, and the link locks itself

The lock is permanent for that link. The page shows the same generic message it shows for an expired or made-up link, so a person guessing cannot tell which case they hit. The only way back is a new link, reissued by Lumina from the Facility record.

08

The view cap is now hard, and a reissue kills the old link

When a link already has ten opens, the next correct code is refused and the link closes with the reason recorded. Reissuing a report, whether by the Resend button or by the job running again, closes the previous live link to the same address as superseded, so only the newest link works.

CaseBehaviourSeen live
Eleventh open attemptedRefused; link closed as View limit reachedYes
Fifth wrong codeLink closed as Locked; the right code no longer helpsYes
Code entered after ten minutesRefused, no strike, back to the request buttonYes
Report opened after the ten-minute windowPage asks for a new code; the PDF address answers 404Yes
Resend button, or the daily job againNew links issued; previous links to the same address closed as SupersededYes, both
Link expiredSame generic page as aboveYes
Sandbox runA code is emailed only to the testers on the redirect list, never to a facilityYes

The Resend button is unchanged, and it is still the route to a fresh link

Staff open the Facility, click Resend Readmissions Report, confirm the addresses, and each recipient gets a brand new link and a new code flow. The previous link to that address is closed as superseded at the same moment. Nothing about the button changed; what it issues did.

Also new on the Facility record: a Readmission Report Links list on the Related tab, showing each link's recipient, role, report date, opens, downloads and status, so staff can see which links are live, superseded, locked or capped before reissuing. Not pictured, because the test facility's rows carry the testers' own addresses.

What a visitor to the page can and cannot reach

Worth stating exactly, because this page is on the public internet.

ReachableOnly when
The facility name and report date on one link rowThe visitor holds that link's URL
A code emailSent only to the address on that row, never to the visitor
The PDF for that rowInside the ten minutes after a correct code, and only while the link is live
Anything else: other reports, patients, facilities, the file listNever. The site user has no access to any of those objects, and the page never asks for them.

Identity is possession of the mailbox at the moment of viewing, which is the same standard Microsoft's one-time-passcode mail encryption applies, plus a record of the device that did the viewing.

Still needed before production

  1. Register Salesforce Sites in production, onceSetup, Sites, accept the terms, Register. A two-minute job for a Lumina admin. The domain already exists. Until it is done every page of the site shows a maintenance message, which is exactly what happened in the sandbox before we registered it there.
  2. Verify the sending address in productionCreate tcm@luminacare.com as an Org-Wide Email Address, verify it, and allow all profiles to use it, so both the report email and the code email come from it.
  3. Confirm the numbers24-hour link, 10-minute code, 10 opens, 5 wrong codes. All are settings or constants that change without a redesign.
  4. Confirm the retention ruleThe stored PDF is deleted once every link to it is dead, after a seven-day grace period. Unchanged from last time and still awaiting a yes.
  5. An owner for the facilities with no contactUnchanged: 159 of 326 enrolled facilities have neither an administrator nor a director-of-nursing email on file. No delivery method fixes that.
  6. Compliance sign-off in writingPossession of the mailbox at view time, with IP and browser logged per event. Worth recording rather than agreeing verbally.
